Rashi on Eruvin 68a:10:1.hebrew: עד שלא ימות - דלא נחתא להו טומאה אשאר פתחים. אבל משימות המת, כבר נטמאו הכלים, ולא אמרינן הוברר הדבר דמעיקרא נמי דעתיה לאפוקי בהאי פיתחא, אלא נחתא להו טומאה. ואפי' כלים הבאין (לשאר פתחים) שם לאחר מחשבה טמאים, דכיון דנחתא להו טומאה, תו לא סלקא מינייהו במחשבה, עד דעביד להו מעשה ממש דפתח ליה להאי, ומהני לטהר את האחרים מכאן ולהבא, כדקתני לעיל: נפתח אחד מהן כו':
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:10:1.english: Before [the person] dies - So that defilement did not descend upon the other entrances. But once the person has died, the vessels [there] have already become defiled, and we do not say that the matter has been clarified [retroactively] that from the outset his intention was also to remove [the corpse] through this entrance; rather, defilement descended upon them. And even vessels that are brought there (to the other entrances) after [his] designation are impure, for since defilement descended upon them, it no longer departs from them through [mere] thought, until he performs an actual physical act for them, by opening this [entrance], which is effective to purify the others from that point onward, as was taught above: “If one of them was opened,” etc.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:10:2.hebrew: וב"ה אומרים אף משימות המת - דאמרינן יש ברירה, דמאתמול דעתיה בהאי פיתחא, ולא נחתא טומאה לאחריני, ואפי' כלים דקודם מחשבה טהורין:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:10:2.english: And Beit Hillel say: Even after the deceased dies - For we say [that] there is retroactive clarification [bereira], so that from yesterday his intention was for this opening, and ritual impurity did not descend upon the other [openings]; and even utensils [present] prior to the thought are pure.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:11:1.hebrew: נישיילה לאימיה אם צריכה - לצורכה חמין, נחים ליה נכרי אגב אימיה. דקי"ל: חיה אחר שבעה, אפי' אמרה "צריכה אני", אין מחללין עליה את השבת, אבל עושין לה ע"י ארמאי:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:11:1.english: Let us ask his mother if she needs - [If she needs] warm water for her own need, a gentile may heat [it] for him along with his mother. For we maintain: [Regarding] a woman in childbirth after seven [days], even if she says, "I need [it]," one does not desecrate Shabbat for her, but one may perform [labor] for her by means of a gentile.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:12:1.hebrew: הא אכלה תמרי - כלומר, הא חזינן דאינה צריכה חמין לשתות, דהא צונן נמי אכלה:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:12:1.english: Behold, she is eating dates - That is to say, behold, we see that she does not need hot water to drink, for behold, she is also eating cold food.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:12:2.hebrew: תונבא - אשדורדישי"ן, ואוכלת ואינה יודעת מה:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:12:2.english: A stupor - Estordison [daze], and she is eating and does not know what [she is eating].

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:13:1.hebrew: פנו לי מאני - בחצירו של רבא היו חמין, והתינוק נשפכו חמיו בחצר אחרת, ופתח ביניהן, ולא עירבו שתי חצירות יחד. ולרבא היו בביתו חדרים פנימיים שאינן פתוחין לחצר, והן לצניעות והנשים יושבות שם, ובי גברי הוה פתוח לחצר (*):(*). ותנן במתני': המבטל רשות חצירו אסור להוציא מביתו לחצר, דהא לאו דידיה הוא. הלכך, פינה כליו מבי גברי כדי שלא יבא להוציא משם לחצר, והלך וישב בחדרים הפנימיים, וביטל רשות חצרו לבני חצר האחרת, ויביאו חמין מחצירו לחצירן:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:13:1.english: Clear away my belongings - In Rava's courtyard there was warm water, and [as for] the infant, his warm water had spilled in another courtyard, and there was an opening between them, but the two courtyards had not established an eiruv together. And in Rava's house there were inner rooms that did not open to the courtyard, which were for privacy and where the women sat, while the men's chamber opened to the courtyard . And we learned in the Mishnah: One who renounces the rights to his courtyard is forbidden to take [anything] out from his house into the courtyard, for it is no longer his. Therefore, he cleared his belongings from the men's chamber so that he would not come to take [anything] out from there into the courtyard, and he went and sat in the inner rooms, and renounced the rights to his courtyard in favor of the residents of the other courtyard, so that they could bring warm water from his courtyard to their courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:1:1.hebrew: מה הזאה שבות ואינה דוחה שבת - ואפי' במקום מצוה, כגון לשחוט פסחו, כדתנן בפסחים בפרק אלו דברים (ד סה:):
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:1:1.english: Just as sprinkling is a rabbinic decree and does not override Shabbat - And even in the place of a mitzvah, such as to slaughter one's Paschal offering, as we learned in Pesachim in the chapter entitled Elu Devarim (65b):

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:3:1.hebrew: תרי גברי רברבי כרבנן - כגון אתה ורבה, דדייריתו ביה:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:3:1.english: Two great men like the Rabbis - Such as you and Rabba, who live in it.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:3:2.hebrew: מר - רבה, אין כבודו לחזר על בני המבוי ולגבות:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:3:2.english: The Master - Rabba: It is beneath his dignity to go around to the residents of the alleyway and collect [contributions].

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:3:3.english: They - The rest of the residents of the alleyway do not pay attention.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:4:1.hebrew: אקני להו - משלי ריפתא בסלא בדיבורא, דליכא טרחא, ויהו כולן זוכין בו לשם שיתוף:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:4:1.english: I were to transfer to them - [Transferring] from my own [property] bread in the basket, through speech, as there is no exertion, and they would all acquire [a share] in it for the sake of the shituf [merging of alleyways].

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:4:2.hebrew: כיון דאי בעו מינאי - אם אחד מהן היה צריך לאכול מן השיתוף והיה שואלו ממני, אין יכולת בידי לוותר משלי בכל שבת. לכך נמצא שאין בלבי להיות בו חלק גמור, ובטל השיתוף:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:4:2.english: Since if they would want [it] from me - If one of them needed to eat from the shituf and were to ask for it from me, I do not have the ability to give up [bread] of my own every Shabbat. Therefore, it turns out that it is not [sincerely] in my heart for [them] to have a complete share in it, and the shituf is void.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:5:1.english: Who requested wine and oil - From that of the shittuf.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:6:1.english: A quarter-log of vinegar - [Ḥala means] vinegar.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:6:2.hebrew: בחביתא - באחת מחביותיך, דמידי דלית ביה קפידא הוא, ועיקר שיתוף ביין, כדאמר בהאי פירקא (דף עא:). ויניח החבית בחצר, ויסמוך על רביעית שבה לשום שיתוף לצורך כל השנה כולה, שמניחין שיתוף בחצר:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:6:2.english: In a barrel - In one of your barrels, for it is something about which there is no strictness, and the primary [medium of] merging is wine, as [the Gemara] says in this chapter (71b). And let [the Master] place the barrel in the courtyard and rely on the quarter-log that is in it for the purpose of a merging for the needs of the entire year, as one may place a merging in a courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:6:3.hebrew: אין משתתפין באוצר - בדבר האצור, כגון חבית של יין או פירות המכונסין, אין סומכין על מה שבתוכן, משום דאין ברירה איזהו של שיתוף; וכי מסתפק ממנו, איכא למימר: אזל ליה שיתוף:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:6:3.english: One may not make a merging with a storeroom - With a stored item, such as a barrel of wine or gathered produce, one does not rely upon what is inside them, because there is no retroactive clarification as to which [portion] is for the merging; and when he takes [for his own use] from it, it can be said: The merging is gone.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:8:1.hebrew: כולן טמאין - כל הכלים הנתונין בעובי האסקופה טמאין, ואע"פ שאינם באהל המת, מפני שאין אנו יודעין באיזו פתח יוציאנו, ופתח שעתיד לצאת בו מיטמא מיד. וטעמא ליכא, אלא הלכות טומאה הכי גמירי לה. ואפי' חלונות של טפח על טפח טמאין, דכיון דכולן סתומין, לא מוכחא מילתא בהי מפיק ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:8:1.english: They are all ritually impure - All the vessels placed within the thickness of the threshold are ritually impure, even though they are not in the tent of the corpse, because we do not know through which entrance they will take it out, and an entrance through which [the corpse] is destined to exit becomes impure immediately. And there is no [logical] reason [for this], but rather the laws of ritual impurity were thus received by tradition. And even windows of a handbreadth by a handbreadth are impure, for since they are all closed, the matter is not evident as to which [opening] he will take it out through.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:9:1.english: [If] one of them was opened - Certainly through that [entrance] he will take [the corpse] out.

Rashi on Eruvin 68a:9:2.hebrew: פחות <abbr title="מארבעה">מד'</abbr> על <abbr title="ארבעה">ד'</abbr>, אינו חשוב להציל על השאר:
Rashi on Eruvin 68a:9:2.english: [A window of] less than four by four [handbreadths] is not significant [enough] to save the rest [of the entrances].

Tosafot on Eruvin 68a:11:1.hebrew: אי צריכה ניחממו ליה אגב אימיה - פירשנו בפרק קמא דגיטין (דף ח: ד"ה אע"ג):
Tosafot on Eruvin 68a:11:1.english: "If she needs [it], let them heat [water] for him along with his mother" - We explained [this] in the first chapter of Gittin (8b, s.v. Af Al Gav).

Tosafot on Eruvin 68a:2:1.hebrew: לשבות דלית ביה מעשה - וא"ת: דבההוא ינוקא דלקמן, דאמר להו רבא "נשיילה לאימיה, אי צריכא ניחיימוה ליה אגב אימיה" — כי לא צריכא נמי, וכי לא היה נכרי בכל העיר שיאמרו לו שיחם בשביל הקטן למולו?! ובפ"ק דגיטין (דף ח: ד"ה אע"ג) פירשתי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 68a:2:1.english: "To a rabbinic decree that does not involve an action" - And if you should say that regarding that infant [mentioned] below, where Rava said to them, "Let us ask his mother; if she needs [it], let them heat [water] for him along with his mother" — [even] when she does not need [it] as well, was there not a gentile in the entire city whom they could tell to heat [water] for the infant in order to circumcise him?! And in the first chapter of Gittin (8b, s.v. Af al gav) I explained [this].

Tosafot on Eruvin 68a:4:1.hebrew: כיון דאי בעו מינאי ולא יהיבנא להו - צריך ליזהר כשאדם עושה עירוב, שלא יערב בדבר שהוא מקפיד עליו, כגון אותן דברים שתיקן לכבוד שבת, או אם יש לו ככר נאה שקורין גשטי"ל או פשטיד"א וכיוצא בהן; דאי בעו ליה מיניה ולא יהיב להו — בטל עירוב:
Tosafot on Eruvin 68a:4:1.english: "Since if they would ask [it] of me, I would not give it to them" - A person must be careful when making an eruv not to make an eruv with an item about which he is particular, such as those items that he prepared in honor of Shabbat, or if he has a fine loaf [of bread] that is called gastel [cake] or pastida [pie] and the like; for if they were to ask for it from him and he would not give [it] to them, the eruv is invalid.

Tosafot on Eruvin 68a:6:1.hebrew: ונקני להו מר רביעתא דחלא בחביתא - לכאורה משמע לצורך שיתוף מבוי קאמר, דלעירובי חצירות בעי פת. אע"ג דאמר לקמן בפרק חלון (עירובין דף פא.): "מאן שמעת ליה דאמר פת אין, מידי אחרינא לא? ר' יהושע" — הא קי"ל כר' יהושע לגבי ר"א דפליג עליה התם; ולקמן בפירקא, בין ר"מ בין רבנן סבירא להו דעירובי חצירות אינו אלא בפת, ולכאורה כולהו אמוראי דההיא שמעתא הכי אית להו. ואור"י, דצ"ל דההיא חביתא דחלא דהכא בחצר הוה ולא בבית; דהא אמר לקמן בפרק כיצד משתתפין (עירובין דף פה:): דעירובי חצירות בבית שבחצר, ושיתופי מבואות בחצר שבמבוי, ותרוייהו דוקא, כמו שאפרש לקמן. וכן ההיא דבעל הבית שהיה שותף עם שכיניו לזה ביין כו' איירי כגון דמונח בחצר:
Tosafot on Eruvin 68a:6:1.english: "And let the Master transfer to them a quarter-[log] of vinegar in a barrel" - Ostensibly, it implies that he was saying [this] for the purpose of a merging of alleyways [shituf mevo'ot], since for a merging of courtyards [eruvei chatzerot] bread is required. Even though [the Gemara] says later in the chapter [entitled] "Ḥallon" (Eruvin 81a): "Whom did you hear who says: bread, yes; anything else, no? Rabbi Yehoshua" — behold, we establish [the halakha] in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua over Rabbi Eliezer, who disagrees with him there; and later in the chapter, both Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis maintain that eruvei chatzerot is [made] only with bread, and ostensibly all the Amora'im of that sugya hold this way. And the Ri says that one must say that this barrel of vinegar here was in the courtyard and not in a house, for behold, [the Gemara] says later in the chapter [entitled] "Keitzad Mishtattefin" (Eruvin 85b) that eruvei chatzerot [must be placed] in a house that is in a courtyard, and shitufei mevo'ot in a courtyard that is in an alleyway, and both [rules] are precise [and mandatory], as I will explain later. And similarly, that [mishnah (73b)] of "a homeowner who was a partner with his neighbors, with this one in wine, etc.," deals with [a case] where [the wine] is placed in the courtyard.

Tosafot on Eruvin 68a:6:2.hebrew: תניא אין משתתפין באוצר - וא"ת: ואביי כב"ש, דהא כב"ש מסיק לה?! וי"ל: דאביי לא חשיב הא דקאמר רב אושעיא "הא ב"ש, הא ב"ה", וקסבר אביי: לא נחלקו ב"ש וב"ה בדבר זה, דכמה פלוגתא דתנאי ואמוראי אשכחן לענין ברירה. ועוד אומר ר"י: דאביי הוה מוקים כולהו אליביה, ולמפרע כולן טמאין דאין ברירה; והוה מפרש (כרבה) דמסיק במסכת ביצה (דף י. ולז.): לטהר את הפתחים מכאן ולהבא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 68a:6:2.english: "It was taught: One may not use [food in] a storeroom for a merging" - And if you say: Does Abaye [then hold] in accordance with Beit Shammai, for behold, [the Gemara] concludes it [to be] according to Beit Shammai?! And one can say: That Abaye did not take into account that which Rav Oshaya said, "This is Beit Shammai, that is Beit Hillel"; and Abaye held [that] Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel did not disagree about this matter, for we find several disputes among tanna'im and amora'im regarding the matter of bereirah [retroactive clarification]. And furthermore, the Ri says: That Abaye would establish all of them according to his view, and retroactively all [entrances] are ritually impure because there is no bereirah; and he would explain, (like Rabba) who concludes in tractate Beitzah (10a and 37b): to purify the entrances from here and onward.

Tosafot on Eruvin 68a:7:1.hebrew: אמר רב אושעיא לא קשיא כו' - הקשה ר"ת: דהכא מוקי רב אושעיא פלוגתייהו בברירה; ובפ"ק דביצה (דף י.), וגם בסוף ביצה (דף לז:), מסיק רב אושעיא דפליגי לטהר את הפתחים מכאן ולהבא, דכיון דנחתא להו טומאה, לא נפקא לב"ש אלא בשינוי מעשה, ולב"ה סגי במחשבה. ואור"ת: דרב אושעיא לחוד ורבי אושעיא לחוד, דהכא גרס בכל הספרים "רב אושעיא", והתם גרסינן "רבי אושעיא". ומצינו רב אושעיא שהיה באמוראים אחרונים, בתר ההיא שמעתא דפ' בתרא דביצה (דף לח:) גבי "ליבטיל מים ומלח גבי עיסה", דקאמר רב אושעיא דשפיר עביד, דאחיכו עליה; וביבמות בריש כיצד (דף יח:), על מילתיה דרב אושעיא דאמר "חלוק היה ר"ש אף בראשונה", אמר "מתיב ר' אושעיא"; ובפרק כל הגט (גיטין דף כה.), בעא מיניה רב אושעיא מרב יהודה. וה"ר מנחם מיונ"י פי': דלא פליגי הכא בברירה, אלא לטהר את הפתחים מכאן ולהבא כדאמר בביצה. וה"ק: הא ב"ש, דלא מהניא מחשבה לטהר את הפתחים, ה"נ לא מהני לענין עירוב, ואע"פ שמזכה להו, כיון דמתחילה לא הונח בחבית לשם עירוב; ולב"ה, דמהניא מחשבה התם, מהני נמי הכא. והא דתנן לקמן: "בעל הבית שהיה שותף עם שכניו", והא דתנן נמי בכיצד משתתפין (לקמן עירובין דף פב.): "מניח את החבית כו'" — כב"ה, דלא בעו הנחה לשם עירוב. וניחא השתא דשבק שאר פלוגתייהו דתנאי דפליגי לענין ברירה בהלוקח יין מבין הכותים ובשאר מקומות. ואף על גב דקאי השתא אביי כב"ש, לא היה חושש לכך להשיבו, דבלאו הכי היה יכול להקשות לו: "וליקני להו רביעתא דחלא במנא", אלא לא היה חושש לטרוח כל כך לערב. ואין זו סברא תמוה כל כך אם אינו מועיל זכוי לב"ש אם לא הונח בכלי לשם עירוב, דהא בסוף פירקין נמי פרכינן: "אלא מעתה, הקנה לו פת בסלו ה"נ דלא הוי שיתוף?", פירוש: ולא יועיל שיתוף משום דלא אפקי ועיילי דרך פתחים למבוי. מיהו זה קשיא: דאדפריך מברייתא דתניא "משתתפין באוצר", הוה ליה למיפרך ממתני' דבעה"ב שהיה שותף עם שכיניו, וכמה משניות דלא בעו הנחה בכלי לשם עירוב! ועוד קשיא: דמה ענין מחשבה לטהר את הפתחים למחשבה דעירוב:
Tosafot on Eruvin 68a:7:1.english: Rav Oshaya said: This is not difficult, etc. - Rabbeinu Tam raised a difficulty: Here, Rav Oshaya establishes their dispute as concerning retroactive clarification [bereirah]; yet in the first chapter of Beitzah (10a), and also at the end of Beitzah (37b), Rav Oshaya concludes that they disagree about purifying the doorways from here onward — for since ritual impurity descended upon them, it does not depart according to Beit Shammai except through a physical action, whereas according to Beit Hillel, thought suffices. And Rabbeinu Tam says that Rav Oshaya is distinct and Rabbi Oshaya is distinct; for here, in all texts the reading is "Rav Oshaya," whereas there we read "Rabbi Oshaya." And we find [a different] Rav Oshaya who was among the later Amoraim: after that sugya in the last chapter of Beitzah (38b) regarding "let water and salt be nullified to the dough," where Rav Oshaya said that he acted properly, and they laughed at him; and in Yevamot at the beginning of [the chapter] Keitzad (18b), on the statement of Rav Oshaya who said, "Rabbi Shimon disagreed even regarding the first," it says, "Rabbi Oshaya objected"; and in the chapter Kol HaGet (Gittin 25a), Rav Oshaya asked of Rav Yehuda. And Harav Menachem of Joigny explained that they do not disagree here about retroactive clarification, but rather about purifying the doorways from here onward, as he said in Beitzah. And this is what it means: This [opinion, which forbids merging alleyways with stored food,] is Beit Shammai, for whom thought is not effective to purify the doorways, so too it is not effective regarding an eruv — and even though he transfers ownership to them, since initially it was not placed in the barrel for the purpose of an eruv; and [the other opinion is] Beit Hillel, for whom thought is effective there, so it is effective here as well. And that which we learned in a Mishnah later (71a): "A homeowner who was a partner with his neighbors...", and that which we also learned in [the chapter] Keitzad Mishtatfin (later, Eruvin 82a): "He places the barrel, etc." — are in accordance with Beit Hillel, who do not require placing [the food in a vessel] for the purpose of an eruv. And this now resolves well why [Rav Oshaya] left aside the other disputes of the Tannaim who disagree regarding retroactive clarification in "One who purchases wine from among the Cutheans" and in other places. And even though Abaye now stands in accordance with Beit Shammai, [Rav Yosef] was not concerned to answer him with that, because even without this, he could have objected to him: "And let him acquire for them a revi'it of vinegar in a vessel!" Rather, he was not concerned to trouble himself so much to make an eruv. And this is not such an astonishing reasoning that transferring ownership would not be effective according to Beit Shammai unless it was placed in a vessel for the purpose of an eruv, for at the end of our chapter (71a) we also object: "If that is so, if one transferred ownership of bread to him in his basket, would this also not be a merging of alleyways?" — meaning, that a merging of alleyways would not be effective because they did not bring it out and take it in through the doorways to the alleyway. However, this is difficult: Rather than objecting from the baraita, where it is taught: "One may use [food in] a storehouse for a merging of alleyways," he should have objected from our Mishnah of "A homeowner who was a partner with his neighbors," and several Mishnayot that do not require placing [the food] in a vessel for the purpose of an eruv! And it is furthermore difficult: What connection does thought to purify the doorways have to thought concerning an eruv?
